binders: A real number σ is universally quantified in the second conjunct.
hypotheses: In the second conjunct, σ is assumed to satisfy 0 ≤ σ.
The first conjunct has no explicit hypothesis.
conclusions: For μ = gaussianReal 0 1 and X = id on ℝ, the ENNReal infimum LocalDef001 μ X is strictly less than ∞.
For every real σ with 0 ≤ σ, for μ = gaussianReal 0 (σ^2 packaged as an NNReal) and X = id on ℝ, LocalDef001 μ X is strictly less than ∞.
mathematical_definitions: LocalDef001 μ X = inf {t : ENNReal | LocalDef002 μ X t}.
LocalDef002 μ X t means that X is measurable, t ≠ 0, t ≠ ∞, ω ↦ exp((X ω)^2/(t.toReal)^2) is μ-integrable, and ∫ exp((X ω)^2/(t.toReal)^2) dμ ≤ 2.
gaussianReal m v is dirac m if v = 0 and otherwise real volume with density gaussianPDF m v.
ENNReal is NNReal with an added top element ∞, and NNReal consists of nonnegative real numbers.
The function id is x ↦ x.
translation.proposition_plain_english: Both of the following hold. First, under the measure gaussianReal 0 1 on ℝ, the infimum over all nonzero finite extended-nonnegative scales t for which the identity function is measurable and exp(x^2/(t.toReal)^2) is integrable with integral at most 2 is finite. Second, for every real σ ≥ 0, the same infimum is finite under gaussianReal 0 (σ^2), where σ^2 is viewed as a nonnegative real parameter; in particular, when σ = 0 this measure is the Dirac measure at 0.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The universally quantified assertion is stated only for σ ≥ 0, even though the supplied measure parameter is σ^2.
The case σ = 0 is included and uses a degenerate Dirac measure at 0.
The result asserts only strict inequality with ENNReal top; it gives no explicit numerical upper bound, equality, scaling law in σ, or comparison between the two conjuncts.
LocalDef001 is an infimum, so the proposition does not assert that an optimizing scale attains the infimum.
Although every admissible t must be nonzero and finite, the infimum itself can in principle be 0.
If there were no admissible scale, the ENNReal infimum would be top under the supplied complete-order structure, so the asserted strict inequality rules out that vacuous empty-set case.
The moment condition uses exactly exp(X^2/(t.toReal)^2) and the threshold 2; it contains no centering or subtraction of a mean inside X.
Measurability and integrability are embedded in the admissible-scale predicate rather than asserted independently for every t.
ambiguities: The body of gaussianPDF is not included, so the exact normalization and the conventional interpretation of a positive gaussianReal parameter v cannot be recovered beyond the stated with-density construction; in particular, calling v a variance rather than another Gaussian parameter would require external information.
